faqs.q: What should I include on an electrician invoice?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name and license number, the client and job-site address, a dated line-item list of work (trip fee, permits, labor, parts), tax, and a total due. Most states require a contractor license number on client-facing invoices.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate tax automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, tax and total update automatically. Leave the tax rate blank if you are not required to charge sales tax.

faqs.q: Where can I find an electrician invoice example?
faqs.a: This template is a ready-to-use electrician invoice example - it comes pre-filled with sample line items (service call, receptacle installation, panel work, lighting) at typical rates. Download the Excel version to see the auto-calculating subtotal, tax, and total, then replace the sample items with your own.

faqs.q: Do you have an electrical invoice form template?
faqs.a: Yes. This electrical invoice form template is free to download as PDF, Word, or Excel. The form includes fields for business name, license number, client address, line items, tax, and total due - everything required on an electrical contractor invoice.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your contractor board and a CPA or attorney before use.

deepDive.heading: Electrical invoicing: licence numbers, troubleshooting time and the parts nobody sees
deepDive.sub: Electrical work is the trade most likely to be inspected after the fact, and the invoice is the document that proves who did it and to what standard. These are the conventions electricians actually bill by.

blocks.h3: The licence question is state-by-state, and the invoice is where it shows
paras: Electrical licensing is not uniform. California issues a C-10 electrical contractor licence through the CSLB. Texas has no statewide electrical licence — Houston, Dallas, Austin and San Antonio each license locally, so the registration number on your invoice is a city number. New York licenses electricians at the municipal level too, and most states that do license require both a contractor licence for the business and a journeyman or master certificate for the individual.

Print the number that applies to the entity that signed the contract. On a commercial job, the general contractor will compare your invoice against your certificate of insurance and your licence record before releasing retainage — a mismatch costs a payment cycle.
list: Business licence number, not just the individual's certificate
Municipal registration where the state does not license
Permit number on any job that required one

blocks.h3: Troubleshooting is billed as time, and the diagnostic fee is real
paras: The majority of residential electrical calls are diagnostic: something trips a breaker, half a circuit is dead, a light flickers. The first hour is spent finding the problem, and that hour is the product you sold. Bill a diagnostic or trip charge explicitly — typically $75 to $150 in urban markets — and say whether it is credited against the repair if the customer proceeds.

Where the estimate becomes an invoice, the split matters: troubleshooting hours at the service rate, then the repair quoted as a separate line. A customer who sees "3.5 hrs @ $110" plus "replace AFCI breaker — $95" understands the bill. A single line called "electrical work — $480" invites the argument.
list: Diagnostic/trip fee stated separately, with credit policy
Troubleshooting hours before the repair quote
After-hours and weekend multipliers shown as their own line
Minimum charge for a call-out, stated up front

blocks.h3: Materials markup and the small parts that add up
paras: Electricians carry breakers, receptacles, boxes, wire nuts, connectors and a van full of stock that the customer never itemizes. Markup on those parts is normal — 30 to 100 percent on small items, less on large gear like panels and EV chargers, which are often passed through near cost to keep the quote competitive.

Never write "misc. material". List the breakers, the receptacles, the wire gauge and the footage. On a service upgrade the panel, the meter socket, the grounding electrode and the conduit are each a line. That level of detail also protects you: when a customer later claims an outlet was never replaced, the invoice says which ones were.
list: Wire priced by the foot with gauge stated (12/2 NM-B, 6/3 NM-B)
Devices and breakers by amperage and type (20A AFCI, 50A 2-pole)
Panel and service gear by amperage and brand
Customer-supplied fixtures: labour only, installation warranty only

blocks.h3: Code-driven work, permits and the inspection record
paras: A large share of electrical invoice lines exist because the code required them: AFCI protection on bedroom circuits, GFCI within six feet of water, tamper-resistant receptacles, conduit in exposed locations, and the grounding and bonding that nobody sees. Customers experience these as upcharges unless the invoice names the requirement.

Permits and inspections belong on the invoice as their own lines with the permit number. Panel upgrades, service changes, new circuits and EV chargers almost always require one, and the final inspection is what closes the job. When a house is sold two years later, that invoice is the record the buyer's inspector asks for.
list: Code-required devices named as code items
Load calculation or panel schedule attached for service upgrades
